Population
Wisconsin population will increase from the 1970 U.S. Census of 4.42 million to about 5.92 million in 1990 - an increase of 34%. The population increase for the nation during the past decade was only 14%.
Milwaukee County is comprised of 19 communities. The largest is the City of Milwaukee, with 1974 estimated nopulation of 683,148. The population of the seven southeastern Misconsin counties most directly affected by this proposed project is expected to increase from a 1970 total of 1,756,086 people to 2,261,000 in 1990 - a rise of approximately 30%. Presently, about 40% of the state's people reside in these seven counties.

Economic Characteristics
Milwaukee County is Wisconsin's most populous county and is the hub of the state's available labor force market as well as the center of commercial and manufacturing activities. Milwaukee County has over 24% of the state's population, 26% of its labor force and 30% of its production workers. The seven county southeastern region encompasses only 5% of the area of the state but has 40% of the state's population and over 50% of the tangible wealth in the state. This region also contains 42% of the state's labor force and 40% of its production workers.
